question: What is the earth set upon?
summary: Job 26:7 says God 'hangeth the earth upon nothing.' 1 Samuel 2:8 and Job 9:6 say the earth rests on pillars that God himself can shake. The two cosmologies describe physically incompatible foundations for the earth.

reconcile.connective: Commentators read the pillars/foundations language as poetic figure for God's sustaining power, with Job 26:7 giving the literal picture of an earth hung on nothing.

discrepancy.connective: The skeptic Robert J. Schadewald argues the Old Testament's repeated talk of the earth's pillars and foundations reflects an ancient cosmology of a supported, immovable earth, though he concedes Job 26:7 is the verse most often cited the other way and its sense is unclear.

skeptic.name: Robert J. Schadewald
skeptic.work: The Flat-Earth Bible (Bulletin of the Tychonian Society, no. 44)
skeptic.attribution: Robert J. Schadewald (d. 2000), "The Flat-Earth Bible," Bulletin of the Tychonian Society no. 44 (July 1987): 27-39

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871), on Job 9:6
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: JFB treats this exact tension, reading the pillars as poetic figure and Job 26:7 as the literal statement about the earth.

link.title: GotQuestions: What are the pillars of the earth mentioned in the Bible?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment of the pillars/foundations imagery (1 Sam 2:8, Job 9:6) as metaphor for God's sustaining power, not literal supports.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The earth is regarded, poetically, as resting on pillars, which tremble in an earthquake (Psa 75:3; Isa 24:20). The literal truth as to the earth is given (Job 26:7).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly distinguishes the poetic pillars-language of Job 9:6 / 1 Sam 2:8 from the literal cosmology of Job 26:7, the exact tension the contradiction names.
